summary: This document is a hypothesis card (N11) proposing a pre-registered assay to test whether a selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) fails to match methylene blue (MB) in rescuing memory retention on a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic model. The claim is NEGATIVE (predicted failure of MAO-B-i to match MB rescue), grounded in MB's preferential MAO-A inhibition profile and redox-facing chemistry. No experimental data has been generated; the assay is proposed but NOT_RUN, and the key comparison (selective MAO-B-i vs MB on COX-amnestic panel) remains UNKNOWN in the literature.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis Card Metadata
content_blocks.content: Card ID: N11. Status: NEGATIVE (predicted). Target: discussion. Topic: neuroscience-brain. Tags: nootropics, brain-longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Vault hold: no. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Related prior: N5–N10 (N10 is MAO-A complement, not selective-MAO-B COX-amnestic proof). Document date: 2026-09-26.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, a selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) fails to match that rescue — retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). This is a PREDICTION, not an observed result.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: MB restores retention after COX inhibition and is a preferential reversible MAO-A inhibitor (PMID 17721552). Selegiline/rasagiline-class selective MAO-B inhibitors improve aged cognition and related cascades (PMID 26142126) but have no published COX-amnestic retention head-to-head (H2H) vs MB. Two mechanistic framings both predict MAO-B-i underperformance: (1) MB's preferential MAO-A profile means MAO-B selectivity is insufficient; (2) COX-amnestic rescue may require parent redox/COX-facing chemistry not shared by selective MAO-B-i. Competing caveat: underperformance could reflect under-dosing/MAO-B occupancy mismatch rather than true mechanistic failure.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Scientific Context
content_blocks.content: Completes the isoform panel on the Gonzalez-Lima COX-amnestic assay after N10 (selective MAO-A-i arm). If metabolic-memory rescue were MAO-B-owned, a selective MAO-B-i should match parent MB. MB's preferential MAO-A profile predicts MAO-B-i underperforms. If rescue requires parent redox/COX-facing chemistry, selective MAO-B-i should also fail. Distinct from N10 (MAO-A arm), N5 (MAO-A-biased generic WM), N8 (Azure B), and N9 (redox-dead) — none ran a selective MAO-B drug on the COX-amnestic panel.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. N5–N10 do not prove N11: N10 left MAO-B open (MAO-A complement only); N5 was A-biased/generic WM; N8/N9 ran metabolite/redox-dead arms, not a selective MAO-B drug; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated selective-MAO-B failure on COX-amnestic.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue PD: Ramsay is preferential MAO-A enzyme inhibition; Weinreb 26142126 is aged-cognition/molecular cascades; neither is COX-amnestic retention vs MB.
3. Occupancy matching: underperformance could be under-dosing relative to MB's MAO profile; assay MAO-B occupancy/monoamine readout without a dosing card; use the same COX-inhibitor amnestic class where parent MB restores; do not collapse N11 with N10 as already closed. No dosing specified.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Refute if: On the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, the selective MAO-B-i matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (retention Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/MAO-B-occupancy-matched conditions — so MAO-B-necessity for metabolic-memory rescue survives and redox-required/MAO-A-preferential framing fails.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content: Three critical ablations identified: (1) Remove same COX-amnestic/retention contrast of selective MAO-B-i vs parent MB: Without behavioral H2H on Gonzalez-Lima class assay, MB rescue LITERATURE and MAO-B tool LITERATURE cannot show selective MAO-B-i fails to match MB rescue. (2) Remove selective MAO-B identity (selegiline/rasagiline-class) with parent-MB preferential-MAO-A framing: Without a verified selective MAO-B tool, underperformance is just 'weak monoaminergic drug,' not an assumption-kill of MAO-B-owned COX-amnestic rescue. (3) Remove N5–N10≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠failure + MAO-IC50≠brain-PD + occupancy-matching discipline: Treating prior cards or empty PubMed searches as already deciding selective-MAO-B COX-amnestic failure would invent a negative result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Method: propose-assay. Kill cost tier: 1 (low cost). Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. The key H2H comparison (selective MAO-B-i vs MB on COX-amnestic panel) has soft-complete = 0 and remains UNKNOWN in the literature.

key_findings: Core claim is a PREDICTION (not observed data): selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) predicted to fail to match methylene blue (MB) rescue on COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay (retention Δ ≤70% of MB).
Execution status is NOT_RUN — no experimental data has been generated for this hypothesis; the assay is proposed only.
The critical H2H comparison (selective MAO-B-i vs MB on COX-amnestic panel) is UNKNOWN in the literature (soft-complete = 0; adjacent PMIDs 40996208/22536538/41108933 are non-matches).
Literature support for MB COX-amnestic rescue: PMID 12384216 (spatial memory restoration after COX inhibitor) and PMID 21087672 (network effects in amnestic model).
Literature support for MB preferential MAO-A inhibition: PMID 17721552 (Ramsay 2007 — potent reversible preferential MAO-A inhibition).
Literature support for selective MAO-B tool: PMID 26142126 (Weinreb 2015 — rasagiline improves cognitive deficits in aged mice), but this is not a COX-amnestic retention vs MB comparison.
Key competing caveat: underperformance of MAO-B-i could reflect under-dosing/MAO-B occupancy mismatch rather than true mechanistic failure — occupancy matching is required.
N5–N10 prior cards do not prove N11; N10 (MAO-A complement) left MAO-B open; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated failure.
Kill cost tier 1 (low cost); estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; IP class: redox-vs-MAO.
TRL assessment: TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis only, no experimental data generated, assay proposed but not executed.
